title: Make preflight.sh exit non-zero when environments are BROKEN (not only MISSING); validate --lang
change_spec: bin/preflight.sh currently exits 0 for a BROKEN-but-present environment: at the summary (lines 116-160) if broken>0 and missing==0, the broken-warning block (lines 121-124) runs, the missing block (lines 126+) is skipped, and control falls off the end of the script exiting with the status of the last command (the warn, which is 0). run.sh:141 gates the whole run on this exit code, so a broken tool passes the gate. Fix, entirely within preflight.sh: (1) immediately after the arg-parse loop add a source of validate.sh — insert `. "$PMN_BIN_DIR/lib/validate.sh"` right after the existing `. "$PMN_BIN_DIR/lib/requirements.sh"` (line 17) — then after `export PMN_LANG` (line 58) add `validate_lang "$PMN_LANG" || die "invalid --lang (use en|it)"`. (2) Introduce `final_rc=0` just before the summary block (before line 116). (3) Inside the broken block (after `if [ ${#broken[@]} -gt 0 ]; then`, line 121) add `final_rc=2`. (4) At the very end of the file (after the closing `fi`/final `ok` on line 160) add `exit "$final_rc"`. Trace: all-good still exits 0 at line 118; broken-only now reaches end with final_rc=2 -> exit 2; missing-without-install still exits 2 (unchanged); missing installed OK with no broken -> final_rc=0 -> exit 0; missing installed OK but broken present -> exit 2. Update usage() exit-code text (lines 39-43) to read '2  one or more environments missing OR broken'. No control-flow rewrite, no set -e change.
rationale: A preflight that prints BROKEN yet returns success is exactly the dishonest-exit-code failure the Safety Constitution forbids, and it lets run.sh proceed into a pipeline that will crash deep in a step. This is a clear, self-contained bugfix that tightens a contract already documented in usage().
citations: INPUT1 map, preflight.sh correctness_risks[0]: 'BROKEN environments never change the final exit code ... exits 0'
bin/preflight.sh:116-160 (verified fall-through)
bin/run.sh:141 (`|| die "preflight failed"` gates on exit code)
SPEC.md §0.7 'Be honest. Never claim a step succeeded without checking its real exit code'
risk: Low. Only new outcome is exit 2 where a broken env exists — a caller that ignored exit codes is unaffected; run.sh now correctly stops. validate_lang rejects a bogus --lang instead of silently defaulting to English.

title: Preflight probes must verify every load-bearing tool/R-library per env, not just one
area: Framework & Safety / requirements (single source of truth)
change_spec: In bin/lib/requirements.sh each multi-package env probes only one binary (PMN_ENV_PROBE, lines 44-53), so a partially-installed env reports OK and fails later; pmn_stats_r checks only R.version.string, never the R packages that 41_diversity.R hard-requires (vegan, ade4, ape, zCompositions, rstatix, ggpubr) and that notoriously fail to install from bioconda. Extend the probes to cheap compound checks (keep --version for tools already probed that way; use `command -v` for secondary CLIs so a missing-version flag can't cause a false BROKEN): [pmn_download]="prefetch --version && command -v pigz"; [pmn_trim]="fastp --version && command -v fastqc"; [pmn_hostfilter]="bowtie2 --version && command -v samtools && command -v datasets && command -v unzip"; [pmn_kraken]="kraken2 --version && command -v bracken && command -v datasets && command -v unzip"; [pmn_stats_r]="Rscript -e 'suppressMessages({library(vegan);library(ade4);library(ape);library(zCompositions);library(rstatix);library(ggpubr)})'". Leave [pmn_qc], [pmn_metaphlan] (single tool) and [pmn_reports_py] (already imports all modules) as-is. Second, add a source-time consistency guard right after the three arrays are declared (after line 59): loop over PMN_ENV_ORDER and, for any name missing a key in PMN_ENV_PKGS or PMN_ENV_PROBE, print `requirements.sh: <name> missing from PMN_ENV_PKGS/PROBE` to stderr and `exit 1` (this file is only ever sourced after common.sh, so failing here is a clear fail-fast; `unset` the loop var afterward). No package-list or version-pin changes.
rationale: The probe's stated purpose is 'the key tool is actually callable' — currently it proves only that ONE tool exists. The R-library gap is the highest-value: a missing vegan/zCompositions passes preflight then aborts the diversity step after the whole expensive pipeline has run. The consistency guard turns a cryptic set -u unbound-variable into a named error.
citations: INPUT1 map, requirements.sh correctness_risks[0-1] and improvements[0-1] (probe coverage; parallel-array consistency)
steps/41_diversity.R:15,70,150 (requires vegan, zCompositions, rstatix at runtime)
INPUT2 vault, Caffrey/tooling note: bioconda R builds frequently miss packages
bin/lib/requirements.sh:44-53
risk: Low. Preflight runs a few seconds longer (R library() loads). No runtime behavior change; only detection is stricter and earlier.

title: Upgrade the automatic human host reference from GRCh38.p14 to T2T-CHM13v2.0
change_spec: Verified accession: GCF_009914755.1 = Homo sapiens, T2T-CHM13v2.0, Complete Genome (live NCBI Datasets check). (1) refs/hosts.tsv: ADD a row `chm13<TAB>GCF_009914755.1<TAB>human (T2T-CHM13v2.0)` and KEEP the existing grch38 row (reversibility / operator choice). (2) bin/run.sh: introduce a single human-label variable just before the host loop (before line 186): `PMN_HUMAN_HOST="chm13"  # T2T human ref for the automatic human-read removal`. Change the extra-hosts skip at line 190 from `[ "$h" = "grch38" ] && continue` to `case "$h" in grch38|chm13) continue ;; esac` (listing either human label in `hosts` never double-adds). In the filter_human block (lines 197-202) replace the three hard-coded `grch38` tokens: `acc="$(host_accession "$PMN_HUMAN_HOST")"`, `--host "$PMN_HUMAN_HOST"`, and `INDEX_LIST+=("$REF_DIR/$PMN_HUMAN_HOST")`, and update the die message to reference $PMN_HUMAN_HOST. Because the index is named by label, the index file becomes chm13.1.bt2(l): 11_host_index.sh builds a FRESH index (its idempotency skip at line 34 keys on the label), so there is NO stale-GRCh38-index trap and no forced deletion. (3) config.example.yaml lines 15-16/22: change the comment 'Human (grch38) is removed AUTOMATICALLY' to 'Human (T2T-CHM13v2.0) is removed AUTOMATICALLY (removes centromeric/satellite reads that survive GRCh38 and get misclassified as microbial)'. (4) Docs: update the grch38 mentions in SPEC.md §2.2 (line 67) and README.md to state CHM13v2.0 is the default human reference, GRCh38 remains available as a hosts.tsv row. Reversible by setting PMN_HUMAN_HOST back to "grch38".
rationale: Two independent 2025 peer-reviewed benchmarks (CONFIRMED by the adversarial pass) show GRCh38 leaves a median ~0.08% (up to 2.48%) residual human reads that are misclassified as microbial taxa, and that T2T-CHM13 removes them — cutting false-positive species ~47.75% and, critically for this project's privacy rule, eliminating sex-determining Y-chromosome signal. It is a one-row data-driven change to an already accession-driven, idempotent Bowtie2 index build; zero new tools/deps.

title: Capture per-pass Bowtie2 host-removal stats into the existing MultiQC report
area: Host depletion / QC, observability, honest reporting
change_spec: Today steps/21_hostfilter.sh sends the SAM to /dev/null and lets Bowtie2's alignment summary (the 'overall alignment rate' = host fraction) go to the terminal, where it is lost; MultiQC (steps/22_multiqc.sh, run over $PMN_WORK_DIR) therefore shows nothing about host removal. Make it observable with an additive capture: (1) steps/21_hostfilter.sh — add a `--log-dir DIR` option to the arg loop (default empty), validate it with `validate_path_safe "$LOGDIR"` when non-empty, set `LOGDIR="${LOGDIR:-$OUT}"`, `mkdir -p "$LOGDIR"`. In run_pass() append a stderr redirect to each bowtie2 invocation (lines 88-92): `... -S /dev/null 2> "$LOGDIR/${SAMPLE}.${idxname}.bowtie2.log" || return 1`. The per-pass, per-host log now contains the summary MultiQC's Bowtie2 module auto-parses. (2) bin/run.sh — define `HF_LOG_DIR="$PMN_WORK_DIR/hostfilter_logs"` near the other dir vars (after line 120; note it lives UNDER work_dir so MultiQC always scans it even in custom layout) and in hostfilter_sample() (lines 206-215) add `--log-dir "$HF_LOG_DIR"` to the arg array `a`. No change to 22_multiqc.sh (its bowtie2 module already matches on log content). Idempotency untouched: the skip at 21_hostfilter.sh:66 still keys on final outputs; logs are simply rewritten on a real (non-skipped) pass.
rationale: Alignment host-removal has two silent failure modes — over-depletion (stripping microbial reads) and under-depletion (residual host inflating downstream cost 7-20x) — both only catchable if per-sample removal is measured. The stats already exist on Bowtie2 stderr; we just persist them where the pipeline's existing MultiQC step surfaces them. High leverage, ~4 lines, no new tool, and it lays the groundwork for a later residual-host/privacy gate.

steps/21_hostfilter.sh:74-94 (stderr currently uncaptured); steps/22_multiqc.sh:37 (scans work_dir)
SPEC.md §0.7 honesty; §3.2 'give a short comment ... after MultiQC'
risk: Low. Bowtie2 summary moves from console to a log file (still visible in MultiQC and on disk); the pipeline's own info() lines still narrate progress.

title: Tighten validators: require a unit on PBS memory and bound walltime MM/SS to 0-59
area: Framework & Safety / validation (allowlist) — FLAGGED: touches validate.sh
change_spec: FLAG: this edits allowlist regexes in bin/lib/validate.sh; keep it consistent with parse_config defaults and config.example. (1) validate_mem (lines 40-43): the current regex `^[0-9]+([KkMmGgTt][Bb]?|[Bb])?$` accepts a bare integer like `4000`, which some PBS/Torque configs treat as BYTES -> a silent ~4KB memory request. Drop the trailing optional group to REQUIRE a unit: `[[ "$m" =~ ^[0-9]+([KkMmGgTt][Bb]?|[Bb])$ ]]`. This still accepts 32GB / 512mb / 1tb / 4000b (explicit bytes) and rejects a unit-less number, which run.sh:73 already reports as `invalid execution.pbs_mem (e.g. 32GB)`. The parse_config default (32GB) and config.example (32GB) both pass, so no default breaks. (2) validate_walltime (lines 31-37): tighten the good-case pattern from `[0-9]*:[0-9][0-9]:[0-9][0-9]` to `[0-9]*:[0-5][0-9]:[0-5][0-9]` so `1:99:99` is rejected at validation instead of only at qsub time; multi-digit hours (168:00:00) still pass. (3) config.example.yaml line 78: extend the pbs_mem comment to state 'a unit is REQUIRED (e.g. 32GB, 512MB); a bare number is rejected'. No call-site changes needed (both validators are used only in run.sh:72-73).
rationale: A unit-less memory value silently under-requesting RAM on PBS is a real correctness/expense hazard (a Kraken standard-DB job needs ~80GB; getting ~4KB fails cryptically after queueing). Requiring the unit fails closed with a clear message. Bounding MM/SS makes the validator's guarantee match its documented intent.
citations: INPUT1 map, validate.sh correctness_risks[0] (unit-less mem) and [1] (unbounded MM/SS); improvements 'Memory unit enforcement' + 'Walltime field bounds'
bin/lib/validate.sh:31-43; bin/run.sh:72-73; config.example.yaml:78
risk: Low, but behavior-changing: a config that used a bare-number pbs_mem is now rejected (it was mis-sizing before). Mitigated by the clear die message and the doc note; all shipped defaults/examples already carry a unit.

title: Add phiX174 Illumina spike-in as a selectable host; document the livestock+phiX+human chain
change_spec: Verified accession: GCF_000819615.1 = Escherichia phage phiX174 (ViralProj14015), Complete Genome. (1) refs/hosts.tsv: add row `phix<TAB>GCF_000819615.1<TAB>PhiX174 Illumina spike-in (Barcenilla 2024)`. It flows through the existing chain automatically — run.sh:184-196 downloads+indexes any hosts.tsv row named in `hosts`, and phix passes validate_name (line 191) and validate_accession. (2) config.example.yaml: in the hosts block comment (lines 14-21) note 'for Illumina data add `phix` to remove the PhiX174 spike-in; add `bos_taurus` for beef, `gallus_gallus` for poultry — reference relatedness to the true substrate dominates accuracy'. Keep the default hosts list as-is (sus_scrofa) to stay non-destructive — phix is opt-in. (3) SPEC.md §2.2 (line 67-70): mention phix and the livestock rows as recommended additions for meat/food matrices. No code changes.
rationale: The closest real-world parameter set in the vault (Barcenilla 2024, the exact meat-plant WMS domain) depletes phiX174 + human + livestock; phiX is an ~5kb spike-in present in essentially all Illumina runs and trivially cheap to remove. The pipeline already supports arbitrary host chaining, so this is a one-line reference-data add plus documentation — the architecture already earns it.

title: Optional --very-sensitive-local host-filter preset (opt-in, defaults to current behavior)
change_spec: Add a gated sensitivity preset without changing today's default or the paired-mode handling. (1) bin/lib/parse_config.py: add one line after line 56 (near the host keys) — `emit("PMN_HOST_PRESET", get(cfg, "host_sensitivity", default="very-sensitive"))`. (2) bin/run.sh: after the other validations, add `validate_in_set "$PMN_HOST_PRESET" very-sensitive very-sensitive-local || die "invalid host_sensitivity (very-sensitive|very-sensitive-local)"` (reuses the EXISTING generic in validate.sh — no new validator, no allowlist edit), and in hostfilter_sample() add `--preset "$PMN_HOST_PRESET"` to arg array `a`. (3) steps/21_hostfilter.sh: add a `--preset` option (default `very-sensitive`) to the arg loop; validate it with an inline case-allowlist and map to a single Bowtie2 token: `case "$PRESET" in very-sensitive) BT2_PRESET="--very-sensitive" ;; very-sensitive-local) BT2_PRESET="--very-sensitive-local" ;; *) die "invalid --preset" ;; esac`; then replace the literal `--very-sensitive` in both bowtie2 calls (run_pass, lines 88 and 91) with `$BT2_PRESET` (a single allowlisted token, safe unquoted). Keep paired --un-conc-gz handling unchanged (do NOT switch to unpaired mode — that is a larger change with its own trade-offs; the soft-clipping gain comes from -local). (4) config.example.yaml: document `host_sensitivity: very-sensitive   # very-sensitive | very-sensitive-local (soft-clips partial host reads; slightly higher host sensitivity, ~negligible microbial loss)`. Compose after ACC-4 (both edit run_pass).
rationale: The 2025 benchmark shows --very-sensitive-local yields materially fewer missed-host reads at a quantified-negligible specificity cost (median 5 false-positive reads), which supports the project's privacy goal and lighter downstream read volume. Kept strictly opt-in and defaulting to today's flag so it is non-destructive; reuses validate_in_set so no allowlist surface is added.
citations: INPUT3 T1-2 / INPUT4 verdict PLAUSIBLE (recommended=true): Forbes 2025 Cell Reports Methods PMC12664888 (Bowtie2-VSL benchmark)
steps/21_hostfilter.sh:88,91 (current --very-sensitive); bin/lib/validate.sh:15-20 (validate_in_set); bin/run.sh:206-215
risk: Low. Default path byte-for-byte unchanged; the alternate value is confined to an allowlisted single token in one bowtie2 flag. Verdict notes the profiling-accuracy uplift is marginal, so this is the lowest-priority accepted item.
